greek: Πᾶν τὸ χρυσίον, ὃ κατειργάσθη εἰς τὰ ἔργα κατὰ πᾶσαν τὴν ἐργασίαν τῶν ἁγίων, ἐγένετο χρυσίου τοῦ τῆς ἀπαρχῆς ἐννέα καὶ εἴκοσι τάλαντα καὶ ἑπτακόσιοι εἴκοσι σίκλοι κατὰ τὸν σίκλον τὸν ἅγιον·
hint: The gold worked into the sanctuary came to twenty-nine talents and seven hundred twenty shekels, by the holy shekel.

notes.text: The tallies of the metals stand here; the Hebrew gives them at 38:24–31, before the garments. The order is the Septuagint's own.
τάλαντον, a balance first, then a talent: the plural takes the plural's own a pair of scales, and the singular's senses in the plural.
σίκλος, shekel, Middle Liddell's one translation: plain.
The article makes a noun of the phrase: of the thing of the beginning of a sacrifice.

hint: The silver from the men counted in the census was a hundred talents and 1,775 shekels.

hint: Each man counted from twenty years up gave a drachma, half a shekel; there were 603,550 of them.

notes.text: Middle Liddell's first sense is a handful, then a drachm, a drachma.
Nominative after εἰς τὰς ἑξήκοντα μυριάδας: the count runs on outside the preposition's case.
of twenty years, one translation: plain, the genitive marked, as at 30:14.
